So the rule that rejected the hook must be a deliberate exclusion in newer code (the heal diagnosis cites `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:60-62` and `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:2239-2247`). Options B and C would relax that exclusion, which breaks the issue's "do not weaken the guard" constraint. Option A fixes the conflict and keeps the host-run safety hook out of the sandbox.

Before building the paired path, the plan should read the target branch's `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`, `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh` and `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`. The paired path should only run when the live hook and its `workflow-templates/` twin are both unmerged. The live copy should be copied from the validated template result, and its bytes must match the template. Every other excluded path should still fail closed. A fix on `ai/issue-6529` only reaches PR #6538's reviews once it lands on `main`, because review runs `main`'s helpers.

Q2: The heal could not tell which path was rejected because the run logged no path names. Logging only the repo-relative names of rejected paths is low-risk and leaks no file content. It must be additive: keep the existing `::error::` text and `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK ... reason=sandbox_path_unsupported` line as they are, and keep the fail-closed exit. Before logging, escape or drop control characters in each name so a crafted file name cannot inject workflow commands.

Q3: The manifest is the other candidate cause. It is a generated, sorted, unique-line list, so any unsupported conflict shape belongs in the existing deterministic manifest resolver (`scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh`), with a regression test. Sandbox admission must not be relaxed for the manifest. Only do this if the plan confirms a real unhandled shape such as delete/modify; otherwise the manifest stays as it is.
